invariants: Same native token IDs, positions, masks, subject lookup, full-vocabulary NLL/KL, native owner/context reductions and current||entry KL.
Same requested R=a*u, beta=lambda_norm/a_star, c=.75, all eligible sites including zero blocks, EfficiencyAdam states and castback projection.
Whole logical batch participates in native mean keys and ridge; SUM objective gradient, mean reporting; no request-independent freeze.
Current candidate own lower all-token writes generate upper K; full K/P/actual-state adjoints; fixed entry W/H/teachers/anchors.
Common strict all(J_r<.05) stop, max25 evaluations/24 updates, no backward for accepted stopping or cap-terminal candidate.
Same FP32 materialized weight addition and linear op, FP64 native geometry, same-A backend; no symmetrization, jitter, rank truncation or low-rank forward substitution.
Exact accepted candidate payload commit; final rewrite mean H once per original occurrence; transaction rollback and observer nonmutation.

measured_baseline.note: Components are measured B1; nested solve metadata can repeat cached times and must not be added.

stages.name: resource_bounded_larger_microbatch
stages.contract: Select contiguous row groups from row/token/activation-byte caps supplied by RunSpec. Physical schedule may change but logical B, owner/context identity and whole-B solve do not. Initial release keeps original global row order; no length sorting.
stages.default_selection: Use largest parity-qualified profile within GPU and pinned-CPU working-set caps; no quality metric used. Record selected schedule and measured resource peaks.
stages.OOM: If graph/group allocation cannot fit, discard current candidate temporary state and restore candidate RNG; reduce physical group cap deterministically and retry same logical candidate. No extra optimizer step, history append, data drop, or source/precision change. Actual physical retries are counted.

stages.name: cached_whole_batch_ridge_VJP
cache: Y=A^-1 K if backend uses it
stages.formula: Bmat=A+K K^T; Z=solve(Bmat^T,G_P); gradK=Z-Z(P^T K)-P(Z^T K). A is fixed; valid for nonsymmetric stored A with transpose solve.
stages.whole_B: Accumulate G_P from all native rows and downstream paths before exactly one VJP per layer/candidate. Native mean VJP retains FP32 nested reductions and FP64 cast.
stages.forward: Keep canonical materialization W_eff=W_entry+FP32(R64 P^T) and actual v=linear(k,W_eff)-linear(k,W_entry).
stages.residuals: Validate primal P once when cache is created; cached identity must match. Validate new transpose solve Z residual. Do not turn mandatory numerical checks off for speed.
stages.cache_scope: Entry A factors persist only with same W/H/profile. First-site K/P reuse requires adapter proof and identity. Upper-layer K/P caches belong to candidate lower-update state and are never reused stale.
stages.transpose_backend: If fixed-A inverse apply is qualified, Z=solve(A^T,G_P-K(P^T G_P)) reuses the entry A transpose factor and cached P; no new primal P solve or candidate B factorization. Validate Bmat^T Z-G_P. Singular A or failed residual uses the same native Bmat transpose-factor backend, never jitter/symmetrization.

stages.name: first_site_no_unused_key_adjoint
stages.contract: If adapter proves first eligible site K and input boundary independent of all optimized R, compute its full R gradient including incoming downstream adjoints, but do not compute or transport discarded P/K/lower-boundary adjoints. Never skip an R=0 site gradient.
stages.fallback: If causal independence is not proved, retain full path.
stages.telemetry: Mark first-site P/K adjoints NOT_NEEDED, not measured zero; do not claim the old universal K-adjoint audit was run.

stages.name: complete_request_stop_witness_with_bounded_fallback
stages.stop_witness: A request is complete only after all its native rewrite and KL components are available and reduced in the canonical order/dtype. A finite complete J_r>=threshold proves the all-request early-stop predicate false. Do not infer this from norm alone, assumed KL positivity or partial rows.
stages.numerical_decisions: Unchanged-group graph/no-grad loss parity is qualified explicitly. New microbatch schedules use declared loss tolerances. Near a stop boundary, before any backward/acceptance, run the original no-grad reference schedule to resolve all-request stop. The guard is based on propagated per-owner loss tolerances, fixed before testing; it is not a new scientific stopping threshold.
stages.boundary_guard: delta_J=abs_error_budget_NLL+lambda_K*abs_error_budget_KL+abs_error_budget_norm. A candidate requiring numerical fallback is reevaluated on reference schedule, with original native stop predicate. If no deterministic parity contract exists for an adapter, use original two-pass path.
stages.memory: Separate caps for live group, pending GPU graphs, pinned CPU graphs, builder boundary storage and factor caches. Activation checkpoint/offload may reduce memory but adds replay; record it and do not count it as eliminated FLOPs.
stages.expected_B1_scope: There is evidence early complete-request failure witnesses are likely (norm alone exceeded threshold in the measured saturated B1), but runtime uses observed full J and has an exact all-pass fallback.
stages.speedup: NOT_MEASURED. Current B1 24 duplicated initial forwards total~224.8s; ~4/350 original groups per probe would cost~2.6s under uniform-cost arithmetic. Estimated removable region~222s (~10.9% fit), not a measured speedup. Other optimizations must be measured separately.
stages.preferred_initial_mode: R4a: original-no-grad complete-owner probe; no large pending graph store.
probe_algorithm: Cap terminal: original full native no-grad evaluation, zero backward.

Pick one deterministic owner from current requested norm penalty (max, input-order tie), independent of eval labels. Evaluate exactly the original physical rowgroups covering ALL native loss rows of that owner, without grad; do not repack/tokenize them.
A finite complete canonical J_owner>=threshold certifies common stop false. Evaluate whole candidate once with forward/backward, accumulate all v adjoints and only then whole-B reverse/update.

If no witness, finish original all-request no-grad evaluation using cached detached probe row values where bitwise reuse is valid, and apply original stop/replay rule. Never freeze an owner based on its own result.

Same candidate and original no-grad witness values are authoritative. Qualify grad-enabled/no-grad loss parity; on unqualified profiles or discrepancy use the original two-pass path. Candidate-wide duplicated replay equality is replaced only by explicit qualified-profile contract and probe-row checks, never claimed to have been measured for all rows.
Technical nonfinite loss/gradient anywhere discards candidate adjoints; no optimizer or history mutation before whole candidate validation.
stages.bounded_graph_mode: R4b: optional later mode defined by bounded_graph_algorithm; not required for initial implementation.
bounded_graph_algorithm: Cap-terminal candidate is known in advance: evaluate once without graph/backward and accept only after all rows are finite.
Otherwise evaluate ordered groups with gradient recording, retaining bounded pending graphs and detached owner loss values; no backward until a complete-request stop-failure witness is established.

If a pending graph would exceed the configured graph-storage cap, evict the retained prefix graphs, keeping detached values and exact replay/RNG descriptors. At least one current group working set must fit.

When a witness is established, replay evicted prefix groups first, then backward retained groups, then stream remaining forward/backward groups in original gradient accumulation order. Each group contributes its native SUM-loss gradient exactly once.

If every request ultimately satisfies stop, discard pending graphs and perform zero backward. If no early witness fits the memory policy, behavior reduces to the existing evaluate-then-replay schedule.

Collect all native v adjoints and all finite losses before whole-B builder reverse and optimizer update. Late nonfinite rows invalidate the candidate; discard provisional adjoints and rollback without commit/history.
stages.probe_state_qualification: Probing executes selected original groups out of order. Require deterministic stateless eval forwards, or exact original per-group RNG/state replay with no persistent hook/buffer mutation. An adapter lacking this contract uses original ordered two-pass evaluation; OOM RNG restoration alone is insufficient.

cache_identity: candidate R identity for materialized weight/v

portable_rows.forbidden: No owner lookup from global_row modulo a fixed context count; no assumed 100 requests, 7 rows, 5 sites, width4096/14336 or fixed benchmark target lengths.
portable_rows.empty_tail: Empty logical batches are no-ops; unequal per-owner contexts and shorter tails use actual counts and native reduction metadata.
portable_rows.adapters: Current production B1 supports a qualified Llama adapter. Other models/benchmarks require additive-write/key-dependency/native-loss qualifications; design portability is not a claim of current support.
portable_rows.sorting: Length bucketing is deferred. Existing append-in-encounter-order anchors/boundaries make naive sorting incorrect; any future reorder needs explicit scatter to canonical row order and parity.

already_present_not_new_savings: direct R/P gradients avoiding dense dW

physical: no-grad/graph/replay forward groups AND valid-token/row counts
FP32 model and FP64 geometry walltime
telemetry.cost_reporting: Separate row/token work, kernel/group calls, numerical linear algebra and elapsed GPU time; Q is a preservation proxy, not compute cost. Use exclusive timers; nested metrics are not added.

implementation_order: optional R4b bounded-graph streaming after separate qualification
